To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the NOS family in metazoan species has evolved by multiple gene and genome duplications and by changes in protein architecture, 2) the proto-NOS was recurrently duplicated and acquired new structural configurations through the gain and loss of protein domains, and 3) the NOS isoforms in vertebrates evolved from the proto-NOS by a first duplication after the agnathostome-gnathostomate split and a second duplication in early tetrapods.

(i) NOS isoforms are the result of gene duplications, (ii) NOS isoform evolution was driven by changes in the protein structure, and (iii) the three mammalian isoforms are the results of a duplication that took place in the common ancestor of tetrapods.
the NOS family evolved through multiple duplication events in different metazoan lineages.
